sim.title: Sim
sim.definition: The controller that ships, played on the robot's fitted twin over the row's target. It is what the robot should do.

on_real.title: Sim on Real
on_real.definition: The row's target on the robot as found: the controller it had before this calibration and tuning (its board gains and any feed-forward it already carried), with nothing newly fitted. On a pseudo-real row the robot is a hidden simulated world.

tuned.title: Sim on Real (tuned)
tuned.definition: The row's target on the robot after fitting and tuning: feed-forward from the fitted values and retuned PD gains. Every real tuned run shown ran PD and feed-forward only; a pseudo-real row names any integral term its controller has.

hero.h1: Describe your robot in CAD. The calibration comes with it.
hero.lead: Every part in a robot description has a known type: a servo, a gearbox, a camera. Each type knows the models that describe it and the routines that measure them, so the description is enough: sim2real builds the twin, plans the routines your bench can run, fits them, and scores the twin on runs it never saw.
hero.today: Today that holds for the bench pendulum's description, and for the UR wrist rig's CAD bundle through a test-only reader. The BAM arm's description is not accepted yet: its servos are not typed parts.
lines: {=1-DOF} pendulum: {rec.pendulum.recovered} of {rec.pendulum.graded} hidden values recovered. Held-out error in multiples of the run-to-run floor: {rec.pendulum.nominal} with the description's values, {rec.pendulum.fitted} after fitting.

UR wrist rig: {rec.urwrist.recovered} of {rec.urwrist.graded} graded values recovered, {rec.urwrist.not_identified} more not identified. Tool error at stops on held-out runs (p95): {rec.urwrist.nominal} with the description's values, {rec.urwrist.fitted} after fitting.

rows.title: {=1-DOF} pendulum on the bench
rows.target: Swings to a commanded peak speed of {pendulum.target.peak_speed}; worst tool error at a stop, stops played, joint tracking RMS. The rounds are matched by peak speed only: the notes say what differs.

controller.words: the fitted twin under the tuned controller
controller.label: pendulum.sim.twin

controller.words: board PD retuned, with fitted gravity, inertia and friction feed-forward
controller.label: pendulum.tuned.controller

notes: The two rounds share only their commanded peak speed ({pendulum.on_real.peak_speed} as found). The as-found plays swing to {pendulum.on_real.amplitude} and stop {pendulum.on_real.stops} times; the tuned ones swing to {pendulum.tuned.amplitude} and stop {pendulum.tuned.stops} times.

Twin against robot on the same tuned runs: {pendulum.fidelity.sim_vs_real}, against a run-to-run floor of {pendulum.fidelity.floor}. The as-found round's floor was not measured: its scorer found no pair of repeat runs with the same input on the tick clock (each candidate pair was rejected for its length).
Scored by bam_rack_twin's pendulum scorer, on a branch that is not merged yet.

rows.title: UR5e, in simulation
rows.target: The held-out workspace tasks at full speed in MuJoCo, where the arm has joint friction its controller's model lacks and inertia it gets wrong. The share of runs (every repeat counts) with every stop within the gate, then medians over {ur5e.tasks} tasks of each task's worst stop and of TCP tracking RMS. No joint error is recorded for this row.

sim.why: arm_motion_bench plays this hidden world only, never a fitted twin of it; its perfect-model run is a frictionless ceiling, not this robot.

rows.title: UR wrist test rig
rows.target: Three wrist joints returning to the park pose {urwrist.tuned.stops} times on a held-out tape; worst and median tool error at a stop, and the stops within the gate. No joint error is recorded for this row.

controller.words: gains and Coulomb feed-forward from an earlier fit of this rig
controller.label: urwrist.on_real.run

controller.words: the same, with one joint's hold gain at {urwrist.tuned.kp_hold}
controller.label: urwrist.tuned.run

notes: Every stop here is a return to the park pose. The as-found controller was already the product of an earlier fit: its gains, and a Coulomb feed-forward on all three joints ({urwrist.on_real.coulomb_ff_can14}, {urwrist.on_real.coulomb_ff_can15} and {urwrist.on_real.coulomb_ff_can16}). Tuning changed only one joint's hold gain.
Retired after this campaign; its design is now the BAM arm's wrist.

rows.title: BAM arm (five-bar, UR wrist, claw)
rows.target: The development workspace tape at {bamarm.target.speed} of full speed; median tool error at a stop (the only stop number this file records per run), TCP tracking RMS, worst-joint tracking RMS.

sim.why: the twin has not been played with the measured static load at rest that the tuned controller adds.

controller.words: the trajectory controller as found: board PD with gravity compensation
controller.label: bamarm.on_real.layout

controller.words: model feed-forward with lookahead, the measured static load held at rest, and a stiffer hold; the boards' integral gain at zero
controller.label: bamarm.tuned.layout

notes: Picked by a stated rule, not by hand: the newest run at this speed with model feed-forward and no integrator. It was tuned on this same tape: the static load it holds at rest was measured on earlier runs of it.

The tuned run shown ran PD and feed-forward only: its notes say the boards ran with integral gain zero. One run in the same file added a rest integrator; it is left out under that rule, but it is one of the earlier runs the static load was measured on.

The twin's nearest run (the same feed-forward and stiffer hold, without the static load): {bamarm.twin_nearest.tcp_rms} tracking, {bamarm.twin_nearest.stop_median} median stop ({gate:bamarm.twin_nearest.stop_median}).

This file records only each run's median stop. PID tuna's workspace sweep, a different target, records every stop: worst {bamarm.sweep.stop_worst} over {bamarm.sweep.stops} stops ({gate:bamarm.sweep.stop_worst}).
A running job still adds rows to this file; the page cites a frozen copy of it.

modes.title: Start in sim at the right values and see the performance
modes.what: Not a sim2real call yet, on any robot. The Sim column above was played by each robot's own lab twin. The missing verb: play a target on the twin under the controller you ship, and score it with the robot's own ruler.

pendulum.why: `simulate()` plays a free release, not a target; the lab's scorer plays targets on its own twin.

ur_arm.why: the wrist rig has no `simulate()` yet; the UR5e is played in arm_motion_bench, not as a sim2real twin.

bam_arm.why: no RobotTwin for the BAM arm yet; its sims run in arm_motion_bench.

modes.title: Run every routine and check it recovers the true values
modes.what: The twin calibrates against a sealed world whose values differ from its description's, then each recovered value is checked against the hidden one.

pendulum.why: every hidden value recovered (the table below).

ur_arm.why: the wrist rig through `sim2real.examples.ur_wrist_test_rig()`; the UR5e only through the sysid oracle.

bam_arm.why: no hidden-truth world for the BAM arm yet.

modes.title: Pseudo-real: another sim with slightly different values
modes.what: Move the hidden world away from the description with `move_truth=`: a fit that misses the moved values must turn red.

pendulum.why: the sealed world, and the description's own world moved by `move_truth`.

ur_arm.why: the wrist rig's sealed world, and its CAD bundle moved through a test-only reader; the UR5e's sysid hidden world.

bam_arm.why: only its homing plant hides values; no `calibrate()` world yet.

lifecycle.lead: Once a robot is at work, calibration is mostly watching the fit. Its own work, every pick, is data. The twin replays recent runs; when the fit drifts it refits a challenger on recent sessions, scores it against the twin in service on the same held-out runs, and keeps it only if it wins. Nothing is installed on its own.

today.text: Live re-identification while the joint works; its page shows its grades, biased against a Stribeck truth.

A gap check every {life.wear.check_every_h} with a wear forecast. In a sim study on the pendulum's hidden world the fidelity ratio warned at {life.wear.ratio_alarm_h} and the gap check alone at {life.wear.gap_alarm_h}; the hidden wear crossed its allowance at {life.wear.crossing_h}. At {life.wear.predicted_at_h} the forecast named {life.wear.predicted_crossing_h}, with plan-by {life.wear.plan_by_h}.
Camera pose refit from belt tags. In a sim study of a two-arm cell, a camera knocked at {life.camera.knock_h} was flagged at {life.camera.alarm_h}.
`Budget(settings=("deployed",))` plans the routines that run on a robot at work plus those that run anywhere, and `calibrate(data=…)` refits on runs the twin already holds.
Each calibration writes a ledger with a W&B copy, and `preflight()` checks a fit before it ships.
No robot has a real deployed record yet.
